name: Motorcycle
description: A motor vehicle, other than a tractor or moped, with a rider's saddle and no more than three wheels on the ground: an electric two-wheeler that can top 30 mph or has a motor over 5 brake horsepower (about 3,750 W) is a motorcycle. Texas has no separate motor-driven cycle category.

restrictions.rule: A rider's saddle and no more than three wheels on the ground (Texas Transportation Code §541.201(9))
Anything faster than a moped's 30 mph or with a motor over 5 brake horsepower (about 3,750 W) (Texas Transportation Code §541.201(9))
Riders need a Class M license, which requires completing a DPS-approved motorcycle operator training course
Riders 15 to 17 who've completed the course can get a restricted Class M license, limited to 250 cc until 16
Riders and passengers must wear a motorcycle helmet, unless 21 or older and either trained in an approved motorcycle safety course or covered by health insurance for motorcycle crash injuries
Registered with the Texas DMV for $30 a year, and must carry liability insurance
Carries a passenger only if built for one, with footrests and handholds, and never one under 5 except in a sidecar
